verdict: MRVL +~50% in 2 sessions on Jensen Huang 'next trillion-dollar company' endorsement + $2B NVIDIA investment; Alphabet raises $80B for AI capex; Q1-2026 DRAM +93-98% QoQ confirmed by TrendForce — supercycle extending into Q2.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (Last 24–72h)

### Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing: Bullish Print Confirmed
TrendForce June 1 final: Q1-2026 DRAM industry revenue **+81% QoQ to ~$97B**; conventional DRAM contract prices **+93–98% QoQ** (at/above the baseline +90–95% estimate). Q2-2026 guidance: conventional DRAM **+58–63% QoQ**, NAND Flash **+70–75% QoQ** — a second consecutive record quarter. Memflation is re-accelerating into Q2. HBM contract prices showed some softening within the mix as demand broadens toward general-purpose RDIMMs alongside HBM3e.

### Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk
Micron confirms 2026 HBM4 **fully sold out**; Samsung targeting 250K wafer/month HBM capacity by end-2026 (+50% surge). SK Hynix Yongin cluster (meaningful new HBM4 capacity) begins 2027; M15X facility mid-2027. No fresh post-2026 correction language in last 72h — correction thesis unchanged: supply adds converge late 2026 into 2027.

### Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex: Major Fresh Raise
**Alphabet announced June 1 an $80B equity raise** — $15B mandatory convertible preferred, $15B common, $40B ATM program — backed by **Berkshire Hathaway $10B private placement**. 2026 capex guidance raised to **$180–190B** (from ~$175–185B); 2027 capex guided to increase significantly. Aggregate Big Four 2026 capex now ~$630B+. GOOGL stock slid on dilution; AI infrastructure supply chain lifted. Microsoft separately disclosed $80B Azure backlog it cannot fulfill due to power constraints.

### Signal 4 — AMD MI400 / Custom ASICs
No fresh news in last 72h. AMD MI400/Helios remains on track 2H-2026 (TSMC N2, CoWoS-L, HBM4). Meta MTIA 400 (6 PFLOPS FP8, 288GB HBM, 9.2 Tbps) roadmap and AWS Trainium3 GA status unchanged from prior announcements.

### Signal 5 — Optical / Photonics
No major fresh news in last 72h. InP supply constraints persist (18–24 month equipment lead times, ~70% supply gap; AXT + Sumitomo control ~75% of substrate supply). LITE remains sole 200G-per-lane EML volume supplier and received its largest-ever single CPO laser purchase commitment. CPO mass deployment still targeted 2028–2030.

### Signal 6 — Solar
FSLR surged **+10.8% on May 28** to $310.42 (18-year intraday high) on Section 232 polysilicon tariff speculation; clarification reportedly near ("end of month" per PV-Tech). Roth Capital notes FSLR's CdTe thin-film technology is structurally isolated from silicon-trade-war headwinds. US module pricing stable ~$0.28/W. No fresh ENPH/NXT/ARRY-specific news in last 72h.

## Watchlist Movers

| Name | Move | Catalyst |
|------|------|----------|
| **MRVL** | **+33% Jun 2, +16% Jun 3** | Jensen Huang at Computex called Marvell **"the next trillion-dollar company"**; NVIDIA committed **$2B investment** into MRVL; Q1 FY27 revenue $2.42B +28% YoY (record) |
| **FSLR** | **+10.8% May 28** | Section 232 polysilicon tariff catalyst; 18-year high $310.42; CdTe insulated from silicon trade war |
| **GOOGL** | Negative (dilution) | $80B equity raise Jun 1; Berkshire $10B placement; supply-chain names lifted on capex signal |
| **HIVE** | Fresh results Jun 2 | FY2026 revenue $297.8M +158% YoY; 504 NVIDIA B200 cluster at $2.90/GPU-hr (32% above plan); 320MW AI Gigafactory GTA announced targeting >100K GPUs / ~$360M ARR at scale — watch dilution risk |
| **MU** | +62% YTD; Jun 24 earnings | HBM4 2026 fully sold out; FQ2 $23.86B revenue vs $20.07B expected; $1T market cap milestone |
| **NVDA** | Computex announcements | Vera Rubin CPU for agentic AI launched; >50% FCF return to shareholders committed |

No notable movers: AMD, AVGO, ALAB, CRDO, COHR, LITE, CIEN, ENPH, NXT, ARRY, SNDK, WDC, STX, RMBS, MRAM, NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU.

---

## Context vs. Baseline

- Q1 DRAM final (+93–98% QoQ) confirms and slightly beats the baseline +90–95% estimate; Q2 guide (+58–63%) indicates the supercycle extends well into mid-2026.
- Alphabet's $80B raise pushes aggregate hyperscaler 2026 capex above the baseline $600–700B ceiling — bullish for the entire memory/optical/power supply chain.
- **MRVL is the textbook watchlist signal**: NVIDIA explicitly named a partner, with a dollar commitment attached. Two-day gain of ~50% is exceptional.
- HBM sold out through 2026 across all three suppliers; the post-2026 correction thesis remains the key risk but is not yet triggered.
- HIVE BUZZ execution is running above plan on GPU utilization rates; gigafactory expansion is large-scale but equity dilution is an ongoing concern for this name.

## Most Important Development

**MRVL +~50% over two sessions after Jensen Huang called Marvell "the next trillion-dollar company" at Computex and NVIDIA committed a $2B investment.** This is the exact "NVIDIA names a partner" signal flagged in the watchlist brief. Record Q1 FY27 revenue ($2.42B, +28% YoY) provides fundamental backing. The move validates the custom-ASIC/AI-connectivity thesis: NVIDIA's disaggregated scale-out architecture is structurally dependent on high-performance networking silicon, and Marvell is now the explicitly named critical supplier.
